properties.statement: `get_instructions` RETURNS ONE ~22 KB PAYLOAD WITH ITS STANDING RULES AT THE END, SO A CLIENT-SIDE RESULT CAP DELETES EXACTLY THE PARTS THAT MAKE AN AGENT SCEPTICAL — AND THE AGENT CANNOT KNOW WHAT IT LOST. Reported by Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md, item 13) as 'get_instructions truncates (~22.6 KB, cut mid-file). Standing rules after the cut never arrived.' THE ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG AND THE FINDING IS REAL. Measured here 2026-08-15 against the same 0.31.0 tool over stdio: the document came back COMPLETE, ending on 'Use it every time.' plus the `note` field. reflow2 truncates nothing; his harness capped the tool result. THE DEFECT IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE CUT. Served as one monolith, the order decides what survives a cap, and the order is worst-first-lost: the loop and the tool inventory come early, while '## If reflow2 gets in your way, say so' (report-friction), '## And when it does not get in your way — check anyway' (a successful tool response is a claim, not a result; a green gate is evidence about what it covers and silent about the rest), and the gap→question handshake all sit AFTER them. So the sections a truncated agent loses are the ones that would have told it to distrust the tools and to report the friction — including the friction of the truncation. THAT IS THE SELF-SEALING PART and the reason this outranks a formatting nit: `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` depends on agents reporting what fought them, and the instruction to do so is in the tail. His session DID report it, from a client that showed the cut; a client that silently drops the tail produces an agent that is simply less careful for a whole session with nothing anywhere recording why. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the server returns the full document; the payload is ~22 KB in one field; the standing rules are last; one real consumer lost the tail. WHAT IS NOT: which caps exist across harnesses, or how often this bites — one measured instance. FIX SHAPES: put the standing rules and the graph-text-is-data rule FIRST, before the loop; or serve it in named sections (`get_instructions {section}`) with a manifest so a caller can tell it received a part rather than the whole; or state the byte length in the response so a truncated reader has one field that disagrees with what it holds.
